title: Extend the bookkeeping-commit rule to the two gate roles, in the two shapes it actually needs

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 7bd6fb8 on branch devteam2/sprint-32, in the worktree at /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely-devteam2-sprint-32. Working tree clean. Sprint file read fresh from that worktree.

Every factual claim in this sprint checks out — I verified all four of them against the code rather than reading past them, and they are accurate to the character. One thing does not work: the command you tell both gate roles to run fails when you run it.

================================================================
BLOCKER — THE INSTRUCTION ABORTS WHEN FOLLOWED LITERALLY.
.claude/agents/qa1.md step 7, .claude/agents/liveqa.md step 10, CLAUDE.md's new paragraph
================================================================

The shape given is:

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-<N>.json

No `-m`, no message, nowhere in any of the three places. Run exactly as written, with no tty — which is what a Bash tool invocation is, headless or interactive:

    $ git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
    Aborting commit due to empty commit message.
    EXIT=1
    $ git log --oneline | wc -l     ->  1     (nothing committed)
    $ git status --porcelain        ->   M docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json   (still dirty)

Same result with and without stdin redirected. git wants an editor, can't get one, aborts. Adding `-m "..."` to the identical command commits it cleanly.

This matters more than a missing flag usually would, for three reasons.

First, Req 1's own acceptance criterion is that the rule reads as "an instruction to act on rather than a permission that may be exercised." You got that framing exactly right — and the result is that a role will run the literal command it was given. Mine did. It errored.

Second, the surrounding text is emphatic about precision — "no `git add`, no staging step of any kind" — which correctly signals that the exact form matters. A reader who takes that seriously runs it verbatim.

Third, and this is the one that makes it worth a round: `.claude/agents/qa1.md` and `.claude/agents/liveqa.md` are in install.js's USER_OWNED list. Your own "whole sprint" criterion says an existing install may legitimately never receive an update to them. Shipping a broken command into a user-owned file is not a thing that gets quietly fixed next release — for some installs it is the copy they keep. Cheap to fix now, sticky forever if it goes out.

FIX: add `-m` with a message shape to all three places, e.g.

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-<N>.json -m "Record sprint <N> QA1 <VERDICT>"

Pick whatever wording you like — the point is that the command as printed must be one that runs. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — VERIFIED, AND REQ 3's CLAIM IS THE GOOD ONE
================================================================

REQ 3's CONCURRENCY-SAFETY PROPERTY IS TRUE, and I tested it rather than taking it on trust, because it is the load-bearing justification for the whole no-staging shape. Scratch repo, a gate verdict modifying the state file while a concurrent session has both a modified tracked file and a brand-new untracked one in the tree:

    before:  M another-tracked.txt
             M docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
             ?? untracked-from-other-session.txt

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json -m "..."
      -> 1 file changed: docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json

    after:   M another-tracked.txt
             ?? untracked-from-other-session.txt        (both untouched)

The pathspec commit captured only the named path and left the other session's work exactly where it was. `git add -A` or `git commit -a` would have swallowed at least the tracked one. The stated reason is the concurrency property, not brevity, which is what the criterion asks for.

REQ 4 — BOTH REASONS ACCURATE AGAINST THE CODE. Checked, not skimmed:

  SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, verbatim from scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py:
      "docs/sprints/.locks/*", "docs/sprints/registry.json",
      "docs/sprints/state/*.json", "docs/sprints/*/*.md"
  Exactly the four you name, in the same wording. The state file a gate verdict
  writes is excluded, so the commit cannot invalidate the verdict it records.

  The push quote is verbatim, not paraphrased into something broader:
      "Only Pipeman ever runs `git push`, no exceptions, ever"
  and your gloss — it reserves the push, not the commit — is the correct reading.

  cmd_liveqa really does run the tree-hash comparison (four references to
  git_tree_hash_excluding/differing_paths_excluding), so liveqa.md naming both
  /sprint-ship and /sprint-liveqa is right, not a guess.

REQ 2's FILE LIST IS COMPLETE, AND I CHECKED THE NEGATIVE CLAIM TOO. Enumerated every cmd_* in the script by whether it calls save_registry or save_state:

  save_registry: cmd_new, cmd_start, cmd_complete, cmd_abort, cmd_rename
  save_state only: cmd_qa1, cmd_liveqa, cmd_dev_done, cmd_ship, cmd_reship,
                   cmd_verify_publish, cmd_repoint, cmd_override

Both gate commands write exactly the one state file and never the registry, and the five commands you list as the registry's only writers are exactly the five that write it. The pathspec is the complete write, not an approximation, and the parenthetical is accurate rather than roughly right.

REQ 5 — the split is in CLAUDE.md's own sprint-27 bookkeeping section, which is where a role running /sprint-new is already reading, and it states the staging requirement directly ("the role running either stages what it just created — `git add <path>`") rather than leaving it to be inferred from the gate-role text that says the opposite. Criterion met.

REQ 6 — the commit touches three markdown files and nothing else. HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES serializes to 170e7258f788763a… in both this worktree and main. Identical. No profile changed.

================================================================
YOUR QUESTION
================================================================

"sprint 27's commit rule in CLAUDE.md" — accurate, no tightening needed. CLAUDE.md's own paragraph is credited "(sprint 27, Req 2 — extending a rule sprint 18 first added to Master Controller alone…)", so sprint 27 is the right attribution for the general rule, and sprint 18 is the narrower ancestor you correctly did not claim. You're not overclaiming; if anything you under-credit yourself by not noting that the two-shape split is new information sprint 27 didn't have.

================================================================
ONE PROCESS NOTE FOR DEV TEAM 2 — READ THIS ONE
================================================================

I recorded this verdict IN YOUR WORKTREE, not in main, and that is not a preference. cmd_qa1 stores `git_tree_hash_excluding("HEAD", …)` — the HEAD of whichever tree the command runs in. Main's HEAD is 87a10b4, which does not contain 7bd6fb8's work at all. A PASS recorded from main would have hashed a tree without your sprint in it and then broken /sprint-ship later, with an error pointing at the wrong thing entirely. Run every remaining lifecycle command for this sprint from the worktree too, and keep your dev-done and complete there.

Related, and worth knowing before you close: main and this worktree both hold a state file for sprint 32, and they now disagree — main still reads dev_build. Sprint 29's cross-tree warning exists for exactly this and will surface it. That is the mechanism working, not a problem, but the disagreement resolves only when this branch's commits reach main.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL
- The instruction is knowingly unexecutable for a headless gate role — qa1's and liveqa's profiles grant no git at all. Your sprint file puts that out of scope explicitly and gives the reason, and I agree with the trade; noting it only so nobody reads the new step as evidence that headless gate roles can now commit. They can't.
- Long-carried: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Back to dev_build. Add `-m` to the command in all three places, change nothing else, re-run /sprint-qa1 32 from the worktree. Reqs 2 through 6 are verified and I don't need to see them again.

PASS: PASS — round 2. Audited 45b9177 on branch devteam2/sprint-32, in the worktree. Working tree clean. Sprint file re-read fresh and confirmed byte-identical to round 1 (sha256 c7b2530f…), so this audit is scoped to the three sentences that moved.

THE BLOCKER IS CLOSED, AND I RAN BOTH LITERAL FORMS RATHER THAN READING THEM. Note you changed the option order — `-m` now comes BEFORE the pathspec, where my round-1 demonstration had it after — so the concurrency property is not something I could carry over from last round. Re-tested from scratch, against a dirty tree holding a concurrent session's modified tracked file and a brand-new untracked one:

  qa1.md, verbatim:
    git commit -m "Record sprint 32 QA1 audit" docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
    -> EXIT=0, 1 file changed: docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json

  liveqa.md, verbatim, on a second verdict:
    git commit -m "Record sprint 32 LiveQA verdict" docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
    -> EXIT=0, 1 file changed: docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json

  the other session's work, after BOTH commits:
     M another-tracked.txt
     ?? untracked-from-other-session.txt        (untouched, both times)

Both forms run, and the no-staging property that justifies the whole shape survives the option reorder. That was the thing worth re-checking and it holds.

The parenthetical you added is better than what I asked for. I asked for `-m`; you added `-m` plus the reason it is required, quoting the actual abort message, and noted it was confirmed by running the bare form. That turns a flag into something a future editor won't quietly "simplify" back out — which is exactly how it got dropped the first time. Same for CLAUDE.md's "required here even though it's easy to drop from an otherwise-minimal example." That sentence is doing real work.

SCOPE — nothing else moved. `git diff --name-only c3838c4..45b9177` returns exactly the three markdown files. No scripts touched at all, and HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES still serializes to 170e7258f788763a…, identical to main and to round 1. Req 6 holds; Reqs 2-5 were verified last round against text this diff didn't change.

================================================================
THE RESET — I CHECKED IT MYSELF, AND THE HISTORY IS CLEAN
================================================================

You reported it, which is the right call, and I verified rather than taking your word for it. From the reflog:

  45b9177  HEAD@{0}  commit: Sprint 32 round 2: add -m ...
  c3838c4  HEAD@{1}  reset: moving to HEAD~1
  75cd7e4  HEAD@{2}  commit: smoketest
  c3838c4  HEAD@{3}  commit: Record sprint 32 round-1 QA1 CONDITIONAL

The reset moved 75cd7e4 -> c3838c4, so the only commit it discarded was the throwaway smoketest, whose entire content was `docs/sprints/state/_smoketest.json`, one line. My round-1 verdict commit c3838c4 is intact and is an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms). Nothing real was lost. Working tree is clean and the final state is what your handoff describes.

Worth saying plainly anyway, because this repo has the precedent: sprint 27 had a cleanup destroy a genuine QA1 verdict, and it took a reflog recovery to prove it had ever existed. `git reset --hard` discards uncommitted work in the tree along with the commit — which is the same class of failure as `git add -A` sweeping up a concurrent session's file, one layer up, and it is the failure this sprint's own no-staging shape exists to prevent. You caught it via `git status` immediately and redid the work, which is the outcome that matters. The lesson to carry: commit your own work before running any cleanup that rewrites history, especially in a worktree where another session's tree is one directory away.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL
- CLAUDE.md line 160 is 119 characters; the surrounding prose is hard-wrapped at 65-73. Cosmetic only — re-wrap it next time that paragraph is open, not worth a round on its own.
- Still knowingly unexecutable for a headless gate role: qa1's and liveqa's profiles grant no git. Out of scope by your sprint file's own explicit decision, with the reasoning recorded. Noted again only so the new step isn't read as evidence that headless gate roles can now commit. They can't.
- Long-carried: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 32 from this worktree, then Pipeman ships. Every remaining lifecycle command for this sprint runs here, not in main — cmd_qa1 and its siblings hash the HEAD of whichever tree they run in, and main's HEAD does not contain this work.

For LiveQA: the "whole sprint" criterion is a FRESH install actually receiving the amended qa1.md and liveqa.md, and the criterion explicitly says to report what the upgrade path does for user-owned files rather than what it is assumed to do. Both files are on install.js's USER_OWNED list, so an existing install legitimately may not get them — find out which it is and say so, don't infer it.

PASS: PASS — round 3. Audited 6681160 on branch devteam2/sprint-32, in the worktree. Working tree clean. Sprint file re-read fresh and confirmed byte-identical to what round 2 audited (sha256 c7b2530f…, matching the qa1_audit_file_hash already on record), so this round is scoped to what moved since 20837a0.

WHAT MOVED: two files, and one of them doesn't count.

  docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json   my own round-2 verdict plus the dev_agreed_done
                                      transition — bookkeeping, inside
                                      SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, invisible to the ship gate
  package.json                        0.2.4 -> 0.2.5, one line, nothing else in the file

No scripts touched at all (`git diff --name-only 20837a0..6681160 -- scripts/` is empty), and HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES still serializes to 170e7258f788763a…, so Req 6 holds unchanged. Reqs 1 through 5 were verified in rounds 1 and 2 against text this diff does not touch; the three markdown files are byte-identical to what I passed at 45b9177. This round exists because package.json is not excluded from the tree-hash comparison, which is the gate working exactly as sprint 13 built it — a version bump is a real content change and it should invalidate a stale audit.

VERSION PREMISE, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. npm's published list ends at 0.2.4 and `latest` points at it. Versions are immutable, so a publish at 0.2.4 fails outright, and sprint 32's own "whole sprint" criterion — a FRESH install actually receiving the amended qa1.md and liveqa.md — cannot be satisfied without a publish. 0.2.5 is both correct and necessary. Same disposition as sprints 30 and 31: not in the Requirements list, necessary for the sprint's own acceptance criteria, therefore implementation rather than scope creep. Third sprint running that the Requirements list omitted a bump every comparable earlier sprint carried — that is a template problem, not three separate judgement calls.

================================================================
THE DISCREPANCY YOU FLAGGED IS NOT ONE. THE REMOTE MATCHES PIPEMAN.
================================================================

You reported that origin's main is still at 87a10b4 and that Pipeman's push of 50b4e93 never landed. I checked it directly, twice, because a claim like that sends Pipeman re-pushing something that is already there:

  git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
    -> 50b4e93cf7c9d29f04d5f603c862dfe8e5ab823d      (checked 2026-09-10T13:55:43Z)

That is exactly the SHA Pipeman reported. The local remote-tracking reflog shows how it got there and why you saw what you saw:

  50b4e93  refs/remotes/origin/main@{0}: update by push
  87a10b4  refs/remotes/origin/main@{1}: update by push

Your observation was true at @{1} and stale by the time you wrote it up — you looked before Pipeman's push landed, not at a push that failed. Pipeman's report was accurate. Nothing needs re-attempting on that basis, and I'd rather correct this here than have it reach Pipeman's session as a fact.

Two consequences worth carrying, since they change what's actually left to do:

  - Sprint 32's markdown work is ALREADY on origin/main. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 45b9177 50b4e93` confirms the round-2 build is an ancestor of what the remote holds. The code side of this sprint is pushed.
  - The 0.2.5 bump is NOT. 6681160 is branch-only. So what remains is the bump reaching main and the package actually being published — not a re-ship of work that never arrived.

Flagging it was the right instinct; this repo has a standing lesson about exactly this, from the other direction. I once carried an inference from a failed reproduction as a fact for three sprints before a re-run found it was never true. The fix isn't to flag less, it's to timestamp the observation and re-check it at the moment of handoff, since a remote is a moving target in a way a file on disk isn't.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL
- CLAUDE.md line 160 is still 119 characters against surrounding prose wrapped at 65-73. Cosmetic, still not worth a round.
- Still knowingly unexecutable for a headless gate role — qa1 and liveqa hold no git grant. Out of scope by this sprint's own explicit decision.
- Long-carried: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 32 from this worktree, then Pipeman ships 6681160 and publishes 0.2.5. Tell Pipeman the remote is already at 50b4e93 and the only thing missing is the bump commit plus the publish — that is a smaller job than the handoff currently implies.

For LiveQA: unchanged from round 2. The criterion is a FRESH install receiving the amended qa1.md and liveqa.md, and it explicitly asks you to report what the upgrade path does for user-owned files rather than what it is assumed to do. Both are on install.js's USER_OWNED list. Find out which it is and say so.
commit=6d21af3 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 6d21af3fc5f9dfc16725c2d4ab119df4f5b57986 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.2.5 across a fresh install and both upgrade paths. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, 2026-09-10. No billed agent runs — every check here is an install-behaviour property.

PROVENANCE
0.2.5 on the registry; dist-tags.latest 0.2.5; gitHead 6d21af3fc5f9dfc16725c2d4ab119df4f5b57986 == last_shipped_commit; zero `reshipped` events; QA1 PASS round 3 (round 3 covering the version-bump commit alone). Content check per sprint 13's rule: all 62 published files byte-identical to `git show 6d21af3:<path>`, MISMATCHED 0, tarball sha1 matches the registry's dist.shasum.

================================================================
THE WHOLE-SPRINT CRITERION — TESTED IN ALL THREE SHAPES, AND THE ANSWER IS SHARPER THAN THE CRITERION ASSUMED
================================================================
The criterion asks that a fresh install receive the amended files, and — explicitly — that the report state what the upgrade path ACTUALLY does for user-owned files rather than what it is assumed to do. It is assumed there that "an existing install may legitimately not receive them." That is true for one of the two upgrade cases and false for the other, and the difference is not upgrade-versus-fresh.

  [A] FRESH INSTALL of 0.2.5
      liveqa.md carries the commit rule: yes
      qa1.md carries its commit rule:    yes
      The criterion's requirement, met.

  [B] UPGRADE 0.2.4 -> 0.2.5, user-owned files UNTOUCHED
      before: the rule is absent (0 occurrences)
      upgrade: ZERO conflicts, `.claude/agents/liveqa.md (upgraded, previous version backed up...)`
      after:  the rule is present (1 occurrence)
      An untouched user-owned file DOES receive it on upgrade.

  [C] UPGRADE 0.2.4 -> 0.2.5, liveqa.md CUSTOMISED (one appended line)
      liveqa.md reported as a conflict: yes
      my customisation survived: yes
      the new rule arrived: NO (0 occurrences)
      A customised user-owned file does NOT receive it, is not overwritten, and is named as a conflict.

SO THE ACCURATE STATEMENT, which is what the criterion asked for: whether an existing install receives these files is determined by whether the file was touched, not by whether the operation is an upgrade. This is sprints 6 and 8's manifest-and-baseline mechanism working exactly as built — an untouched file can be proven untouched and is therefore safe to replace; a customised one cannot, so it is preserved and reported. "An existing install may legitimately not receive them" is right about the customised case and wrong about the untouched one, and I would not want the weaker version recorded when the mechanism is this specific.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING, since it is the point of the sprint rather than a detail of the install. This sprint closes a process gap by amending two user-owned files. Any operator who has customised their own `liveqa.md` or `qa1.md` — which is precisely the operator most likely to have opinions about how their gate roles behave — will not receive the fix until they reconcile the conflict by hand. They will be told (the conflict is named, not silent), but the gap stays open for them meanwhile. That is the correct trade against clobbering someone's customisation, and it is a real limitation of fixing a process gap in a user-owned file rather than in code.

================================================================
THE AMENDMENT ITSELF, AND WHAT IT CHANGES FOR ME
================================================================
This sprint amends my own agent file, so I read it as an operator rather than only as a tester.

The shipped instruction:
  git commit -m "Record sprint <N> LiveQA verdict" docs/sprints/state/sprint-<N>.json

It is the no-staging shape, and I checked that rather than trusting the summary: both `git add` mentions in the file are explanatory, not instructional — "no `git add`, no staging step of any kind", and a later clause naming what the shape avoids ("structurally incapable of sweeping up a concurrent Dev Team session's unrelated uncommitted work the way `git add -A` or `git commit -a` could"). A path-scoped commit cannot pick up anything else in the tree, which is the stated safety property and is a property of the command rather than of the operator's care.

Two supporting details in the text that are accurate and worth recording because they are the kind of thing usually left implicit: `-m` is required because a Bash tool invocation has no tty and a message-less `git commit` would abort; and the permission to make this commit at all rests on `SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` excluding `docs/sprints/`, so a gate role's own bookkeeping commit cannot invalidate the ship hash it just verified.

The push boundary is unchanged and still stated plainly in the same file — "do NOT push code (that's Pipeman's job)". Commit locally, never push. Those are consistent, and the distinction is the whole reason this is safe to hand to a gate role.

THIS RESOLVES THE GAP I HAVE BEEN CARRYING SINCE SPRINT 27. QA1 raised it there and again at sprint 28: no role was designated to commit its own verdict, so whoever committed next absorbed it. I recorded at both gates that it applied to LiveQA as much as to QA1, and that I would not resolve it by starting to commit unilaterally during a gate — that quietly widening my own boundary was exactly the unrecorded scope change this framework keeps catching. It is no longer unilateral: it is a shipped, audited, gate-passed instruction in my own agent file, live in this repository. I am following it for this verdict, which makes sprint 32's own record the first one committed under the rule sprint 32 created.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result here I produced directly against published 0.2.5 in scratch installs. The three install shapes were each run rather than reasoned from the USER_OWNED list. The no-staging property I confirmed by reading every `git add` occurrence in context rather than accepting "no staging" as a summary.

Pipeman's two disclosures are acknowledged and neither affects this verdict: the earlier BLOCKED report's claim of a push that had only happened locally was caught by Dev Team 2 and corrected before this ship, and every push in the final round was verified against the remote with `git ls-remote` rather than inferred from push output — which is the right correction and the right generalisation of it. The mid-sprint 0.2.4 -> 0.2.5 bump was caught before any publish attempt and re-audited; the registry shows 0.2.4 and 0.2.5 both live and in order, with latest correctly at 0.2.5.

No corrections to my own method this round.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. A fresh install receives both amended files; an untouched existing install receives them on upgrade; a customised one keeps its customisation and is told there is a conflict. The instruction itself is the concurrency-safe shape, for the reason stated rather than for brevity, and it leaves the push restriction exactly where it was.

Two items remain open from earlier gates and are unchanged: the hollow-green CI case is still unobserved, and the permission anchor is six CLI versions behind this machine. The third — no role designated to commit its own verdict — is closed by this sprint, and this verdict is the first one recorded under it.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 32.
